_howto: HR how-to guides (listed under How-to guides in the ? menu). mode click = the user clicks the real button. optional = skipped when that part isn't on screen. Never reuse a step id.

guides.title: Write a contract template
guides.blurb: Write a contract in the editor, with placeholders that fill in each employee's details.

steps.title: Contracts & Onboarding
steps.text: Contract templates live here. Click it.

steps.title: Contract Templates
steps.text: Click the Contract Templates tab.

steps.title: Create New Template
steps.text: Click Create New Template. Nothing is saved until you click Save at the bottom.

steps.title: Template Title
steps.text: The name people pick when they assign a contract, for example Seasonal Worker 3-Month Contract. It's also printed as the contract's title.

steps.title: Imported PDF
steps.text: This template is an imported PDF, so the text editors are switched off to keep the document exactly as it is. When it's assigned, the system adds a cover page and signature block.

steps.title: Translated version
steps.text: Tick this to add the contract text in a second language (for example the employee's home language) alongside the main text.

steps.title: Header and footer
steps.text: The Global Header and Global Footer repeat on every page, for example your company name, a reference number or [Page Number].

steps.title: Contract text
steps.text: Type or paste the contract here and format it like a normal document. Put placeholders wherever an employee's details should appear.

steps.title: Translated text
steps.text: The same contract in the second language, if you ticked the translated version.

steps.title: Dynamic placeholders
steps.text:
Click a tag to copy it, then paste it into the text. When a contract is printed for an employee, each tag is replaced with their details: name, address, PIN, ID number, department, the contract dates and wage.

[Page Break] starts a new page and [Page Number] numbers the pages.

steps.title: Signatures
steps.text: Put [Employee Signature] and [Manager Signature] where each person signs. Their captured signatures are printed in those places.

steps.title: Preview
steps.text: Choose an employee (or leave dummy data) and click Preview PDF to see exactly how the contract will print, with the placeholders filled in.

steps.title: Save
steps.text: Saves the template. It's then available under Assign Contract. This guide hasn't saved anything: click Cancel if you were only practising.

guides.title: Assign and approve a contract
guides.blurb: Give an employee a contract, approve it, and file the signed copy.

steps.title: Contracts & Onboarding
steps.text: Contracts are assigned here. Click it.

steps.title: Assign Contract
steps.text: Click the Assign Contract tab.

steps.title: 1. Select the employee
steps.text: Opens a list where you search by name or PIN and filter by department. You can include terminated employees, for example when a seasonal worker comes back.

steps.title: 2. Contract template
steps.text: Which contract they get. Templates are set up under Contract Templates.

steps.title: Valid From
steps.text: The first day of the contract.

steps.title: Valid To (Auto-Terminate)
steps.text: The last day of the contract. The employee is terminated automatically on this date, and it's scheduled as soon as you assign the contract.

steps.title: Permanent
steps.text: Tick this for a permanent contract with no end date. Valid To is then switched off.

steps.title: Wage (optional)
steps.text: The wage type (Hourly or Fixed/Monthly) and rate for this contract. You confirm them again when the contract is approved.

steps.title: Assign
steps.text: Creates the contract and moves it to Awaiting Approval. Nothing has been assigned by this guide.

steps.title: Awaiting Approval
steps.text: New contracts wait here. Use the icons to check signatures and documents, and the printer for the contract PDF. Approve lets you confirm the department, the employee's PIN (you can give a new one) and the wage, then Approve & Activate.

steps.title: Contracts Audit
steps.text: Active contracts show here. Once the employee has signed the paper copy, use the upload button on their row so it's on file. The Missing Physical Copy and Expiring in Month filters help you follow up.

guides.title: Import a PDF contract and map its fields
guides.blurb: Use your existing contract PDF as-is, and mark where each employee's details go.

steps.title: Contracts & Onboarding
steps.text: Contract templates live here. Click it.

steps.title: Contract Templates
steps.text: Click the Contract Templates tab.

steps.title: Import Contract PDF
steps.text: Click Import Contract PDF and choose your contract. It's stored exactly as it is, and the field mapper opens straight after.

steps.title: Your PDF
steps.text: This is your contract, exactly as imported; the document itself is never changed. Drag a box over each place where an employee's detail belongs, such as the name line, then choose which detail fills that box.

steps.title: Pages
steps.text: Move between the pages of the contract to map fields on each one.

steps.title: Mapped fields
steps.text: Every box you've placed so far, and the detail each one shows.

steps.title: Save Field Map
steps.text:
Saves your boxes. When this template is assigned, each employee's details are filled into those boxes, and a cover page and signature block are added.

You can come back any time with the Map Fields button on the template.

guides.title: Set up infringement rules
guides.blurb: Create categories and the rules (with severity) that infringements are recorded against.

steps.title: HR Settings
steps.text: Categories and rules live here. Click it.

steps.title: Categories
steps.text: Click Categories.

steps.title: Add a category
steps.text: Click to add a category.

steps.title: Category Name
steps.text: A group for related rules, for example Safety Gear, Attendance or Conduct.

steps.title: Applies To
steps.text: Whether the category is for Infringements or Performance Notes. Save it, then carry on.

steps.title: HR Rules
steps.text: Now the rules. Close the category form (Save or Cancel), then click HR Rules.
steps.hint: Close the form, then click HR Rules

steps.title: Add a rule
steps.text: Click to add a rule.

steps.title: Rule Code
steps.text: A short unique code, for example ATT-01. It identifies the rule on records and reports.

steps.title: Category
steps.text: Which category the rule belongs to.

steps.title: Description
steps.text: What the rule is, in plain words. This is what people see when recording an infringement.

steps.title: Severity
steps.text: 1 Verbal Warning, 2 Written Warning, 3 Final Written Warning, 4 Termination / Dismissal.

steps.title: Save
steps.text: Saves the rule. It can then be recorded against employees. This guide hasn't saved anything: click Cancel if you were only practising.

guides.title: Build an onboarding workflow
guides.blurb: Create a workflow, add its steps, and assign it to employees.

steps.title: Workflows
steps.text: Onboarding workflows live here. Click it.

steps.title: Create Workflow
steps.text: Click to create a workflow.

steps.title: Workflow Name
steps.text: For example Seasonal Worker Onboarding.

steps.title: Description
steps.text: What this workflow is for.

steps.title: Routing Mode
steps.text:
Custom / Dynamic: steps go to the new employee, their department's HOD, or a specific person.
System Hierarchy: steps go to the approval levels of a hierarchy from Routing & Stand-ins.

steps.title: Hierarchy
steps.text: With System Hierarchy, choose which approval hierarchy the steps follow.

steps.title: Save the workflow
steps.text: Click Save Workflow (or Cancel if you're only practising), then click Next. Its card then appears in the list, ready for steps.

steps.title: Add Step
steps.text: Each workflow card has Add Step. Click it on your workflow.

steps.title: Step Name (Task)
steps.text: What needs to be done, for example Sign contract or Issue PPE.

steps.title: Instructions
steps.text: How to do it, for whoever gets the task.

steps.title: Responsible Party
steps.text: Who does this step. With Custom routing: the new employee, their department's HOD, or a specific individual. With System Hierarchy: the Level 1, 2 or 3 approver, or the standing approver.

steps.title: Step Sequence
steps.text: The order of the step: 1 first, then 2, and so on.

steps.title: Escalation Days
steps.text: If the step isn't done within this many days, it's escalated. 0 means never.

steps.title: Require Document Upload
steps.text: Tick this if the step can only be completed with a document attached, for example a signed form.

steps.title: Save Step
steps.text: Saves the step on the workflow. Add as many steps as you need.

steps.title: Assign it
steps.text: Finally, on Assign Workflow, choose the workflow and who it applies to: everyone, a department or one employee.

guides.title: Set up approval routing and stand-ins
guides.blurb: Create an approval hierarchy with levels, and cover for a manager who is away.

steps.title: Routing & Stand-ins
steps.text: Approval routing lives here. Click it.

steps.title: Create a hierarchy
steps.text: Click to create an approval hierarchy.

steps.title: Hierarchy Name
steps.text: For example Farm Operations Approvals.

steps.title: Approval levels
steps.text: Click Add Level for each level of approval. On each level, Select who approves: a department (its HOD) or a specific active user. Level 1 approves first.

steps.title: Standing Approver
steps.text: Optional fallback: the person who approves when a level has nobody to approve.

steps.title: Save Hierarchy
steps.text: Saves it, ready for workflows set to System Hierarchy. Click Save Hierarchy (or Cancel if you're only practising), then click Next.

steps.title: Stand-in Management
steps.text: Click Stand-in Management.

steps.title: Assign a stand-in
steps.text: Click to assign a stand-in.

steps.title: Who is away
steps.text: The manager who is away.

steps.title: Who takes over
steps.text: The person approving in their place.

steps.title: From and to
steps.text: The stand-in only applies between these dates. Afterwards, approvals go back to the original manager automatically.

steps.title: Assign Stand-in
steps.text: Saves the stand-in. This guide hasn't saved anything: click Cancel if you were only practising.

guides.title: Calculate KPIs and print a report
guides.blurb: Measure attendance KPIs for a period and print an employee, department or company report.

steps.title: Core KPIs
steps.text: KPIs live here. Click it.

steps.title: 1. Choose the period
steps.text: Set the start and end date.

steps.title: 2. Who to measure
steps.text:
A department, or one employee (next to it), or leave both empty for the whole company.

For a Dept Report choose a department; for an Employee Report choose an employee.

steps.title: 3. Calculate
steps.text: Click Calculate.

steps.title: 4. Read the results
steps.text: The seven KPIs for your choice. Click any card to see how it was worked out and whether it's healthy (green), worth watching (amber) or needs action (red).

steps.title: 5. Print a report
steps.text: Choose Employee, Dept or Company Report. Each prints the calculation you've just made.
